forwardsBanner: **Flexibility over labels.** On the Phins, roles shift with the game. Learn your main job, then be ready to do everything.
backsBanner: Backs cards are coming soon. [HANNAH TO PROVIDE: backs content]

positions.name: Prop
positions.job: You anchor the scrum, one on each side of the hooker. In the lineout you could be a lifter or in the back pod. In open play you're in a center pod and carry the ball in a pod of 3.

more.title: Loosehead (1) vs Tighthead (3)
points: **Loosehead (1):** Left side of the scrum. Your head goes on the outside of the opposing tighthead, so you have only one opponent's head next to you. You keep your side stable and give your hooker a clear view of the ball.

**Tighthead (3):** Right side of the scrum. Your head goes between the opposing loosehead and hooker, so you take pressure from both sides. This is the cornerstone of the scrum. If the tighthead goes backward, the scrum goes backward.
Both props: in the lineout you could be a lifter or in the back pod, depending on the call. In open play you're in a center pod.

positions.name: Hooker
positions.job: You hook the ball back in the scrum and throw in at every lineout. In open play you're in a center pod and carry the ball in a pod of 3.

more.title: Hooker details
points: The throw is the one set job in our lineout: the hooker always throws. It has to go straight down the middle, and the call tells you the target.
In the scrum your props hold you up so you can hook the ball back with your foot.
We use the brake foot rule. Ask your coach to show you the brake foot position.

positions.name: Locks
positions.job: You push straight through your props in the scrum. In the lineout you could lift, jump, or be in the back pod, depending on the call. In open play you're in a center pod and carry the ball in a pod of 3.

more.title: Lock details
points: In the scrum your head goes in the gap between your hooker and a prop, and your shoulders push on the front row's hips. Your power goes straight forward.
Setting your feet: start with both knees on the ground. Only start with one knee down if you have good mobility.
Don't launch forward on "Set." No pushing early.

positions.name: Flankers
positions.job: Flankers are workhorses. You're one of the three forwards not pushing in the scrum, so be ready to hit on defense. On defense at the scrum, get off quickly and put pressure on the opposition. In open play you're usually on an edge of our 1-3-3-1 (sideline to the 15m line).

subroles.label: Blindside (6)
subroles.text: Covers the short side of the field. Watch for the pick and go and the eight man pick from the scrum.

subroles.label: Openside (7)
subroles.text: Covers the open (wide) side. Usually going after their backs on defense.

more.title: Flanker details
points: If the tight five are gassed, you might jump into a tight five role, like a center pod.
Some teams use openside/blindside and some use left/right flankers (each flanker stays on one side of the scrum no matter where the play is).
Talk to the flanker you're working with to see if they prefer a specific side.
But be prepared to do everything!

positions.name: Number Eight
positions.job: You control the ball at the base of the scrum and link the forwards with the backs. In open play you usually join the tight five in the center pods.

more.title: Number Eight details
points: Only the 8 can pick the ball up from the base of the scrum (the "eight man pick").
You and the 9 decide together when the ball comes out and what happens next.
Note: if the usual 8 is out, the shape can shift (see the What If? Lab).
